assets.purpose: How a Go program runs. Source files become a linked executable, which runs with the Go runtime and imported packages.
assets.alt_text: How a Go program runs: Source files; then Compile & link; then Executable; then Runtime + standard library. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Source files become a linked executable, which runs with the Go runtime and imported packages.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Types and zero values. A declared type determines legal operations and the default value when a variable is not explicitly initialized.
assets.alt_text: Types and zero values: Declare type; then Compiler checks; then Zero value or initializer; then Use value safely. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: A declared type determines legal operations and the default value when a variable is not explicitly initialized.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Control flow: decisions and repetition. Conditions choose a branch, while loops repeat a bounded operation until a condition changes.
assets.alt_text: Control flow: decisions and repetition: Read input; then Check condition; then Choose branch; then Repeat or finish. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Conditions choose a branch, while loops repeat a bounded operation until a condition changes.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Slices and shared storage. A slice describes a view into an underlying array; append may reuse or replace that storage.
assets.alt_text: Slices and shared storage: Slice header; then Length / capacity; then Backing array; then Append may reallocate. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: A slice describes a view into an underlying array; append may reuse or replace that storage.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: UTF-8: bytes and runes. A string is a byte sequence. Runes represent Unicode code points, which are not always user-perceived characters.
assets.alt_text: UTF-8: bytes and runes: String bytes; then UTF-8 decoding; then Runes / code points; then Display may combine code points. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: A string is a byte sequence. Runes represent Unicode code points, which are not always user-perceived characters.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Interfaces are satisfied implicitly. A concrete type satisfies an interface when its method set supplies the methods the interface requires.
assets.alt_text: Interfaces are satisfied implicitly: Consumer needs behavior; then Small interface; then Concrete type methods; then Substitution without declaration. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: A concrete type satisfies an interface when its method set supplies the methods the interface requires.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Generics: one algorithm, type-safe inputs. Type parameters and constraints let one function or type work across a permitted set of types.
assets.alt_text: Generics: one algorithm, type-safe inputs: Type parameter; then Constraint / type set; then Inference or explicit type; then Compile-time checking. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Type parameters and constraints let one function or type work across a permitted set of types.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Values, pointers, and reachability. A pointer refers to a value. The garbage collector keeps reachable objects alive, but references can retain more memory than expected.
assets.alt_text: Values, pointers, and reachability: Value; then Address; then Pointer reference; then Reachability controls lifetime. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: A pointer refers to a value. The garbage collector keeps reachable objects alive, but references can retain more memory than expected.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Error context without losing identity. Wrap errors at boundaries to add context, then inspect the chain with errors.Is or errors.As when needed.
assets.alt_text: Error context without losing identity: Underlying error; then Add operation context; then Propagate to caller; then Inspect at boundary. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Wrap errors at boundaries to add context, then inspect the chain with errors.Is or errors.As when needed.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Modules contain packages. A module version describes a collection of packages; go.mod records the module path and dependency requirements.
assets.alt_text: Modules contain packages: Repository / module; then go.mod + versions; then Packages / imports; then Build and test. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: A module version describes a collection of packages; go.mod records the module path and dependency requirements.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: A fast feedback loop. Focused tests, static checks, race detection, and fuzzing cover different defect classes; none alone proves correctness.
assets.alt_text: A fast feedback loop: Write assertion; then Run go test; then Add vet / race / fuzz; then Review missing cases. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Focused tests, static checks, race detection, and fuzzing cover different defect classes; none alone proves correctness.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Bounded concurrent pipeline. A bounded queue and worker count constrain parallel work; context cancellation and error propagation provide a clean stop path.
assets.alt_text: Bounded concurrent pipeline: Producer; then Bounded channel; then Worker pool; then Result + cancellation. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: A bounded queue and worker count constrain parallel work; context cancellation and error propagation provide a clean stop path.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: An HTTP request lifecycle. A handler validates inputs, applies application logic, and writes a controlled response under request deadlines.
assets.alt_text: An HTTP request lifecycle: Request arrives; then Validate / authorize; then Handle domain work; then Status + response. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: A handler validates inputs, applies application logic, and writes a controlled response under request deadlines.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Transaction: commit all or roll back. Use parameterized statements and a transaction so related changes succeed together or are reverted together.
assets.alt_text: Transaction: commit all or roll back: Begin transaction; then Parameterized queries; then Check every error; then Commit or rollback. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Use parameterized statements and a transaction so related changes succeed together or are reverted together.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Secure request boundaries. Treat external input as untrusted; validate, authorize, bound resource use, and avoid leaking secrets in errors or logs.
assets.alt_text: Secure request boundaries: Untrusted input; then Validate & authorize; then Bound resources; then Safe output / logs. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Treat external input as untrusted; validate, authorize, bound resource use, and avoid leaking secrets in errors or logs.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Observe, diagnose, improve. Logs provide event detail, metrics reveal trends, and traces connect work across boundaries; correlate them with identifiers.
assets.alt_text: Observe, diagnose, improve: Instrument; then Collect logs / metrics / traces; then Investigate signal; then Improve and verify. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Logs provide event detail, metrics reveal trends, and traces connect work across boundaries; correlate them with identifiers.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: A dependable release pipeline. Build, test, analyze, scan, package, deploy, verify, and retain a safe rollback path.
assets.alt_text: A dependable release pipeline: Format / build; then Test / vet / scan; then Create artifact; then Deploy / observe / rollback. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Build, test, analyze, scan, package, deploy, verify, and retain a safe rollback path.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.

assets.purpose: Cancellation follows the work. Pass context across request and job boundaries so deadlines and cancellation can stop work and release resources.
assets.alt_text: Cancellation follows the work: Parent context; then Deadline / cancel; then Propagate to calls; then Stop work and clean up. Each phase is labeled with text and ordered left to right.
assets.caption: Pass context across request and job boundaries so deadlines and cancellation can stop work and release resources.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf educational diagram generated for this Go course.
